scenes.title: Facebook leads already in GoHighLevel
scenes.page: Lesson 2 • Keep your existing Facebook connection
scenes.narration: If your Facebook or Instagram form leads already arrive in Go High Level, we can keep that working connection and add Patient Pipeline after it. That's what we'll do together in this lesson. You don't need to disconnect Facebook or rebuild your existing follow-up. We'll create the campaign, add a separate sending workflow, and follow a new submission through both systems so you know where to check. The outside screens are instructional recreations, not recordings of your account. Pause whenever you need to catch up, and use the matching controls in your own account.

fields.label: Before starting
fields.value: New Instant Form leads already arrive in the correct practice

scenes.checkpoint: If leads do not reach GoHighLevel, this is not your route.

scenes.title: Before we begin
scenes.narration: Before we get into the setup, have your actual offer handy. We'll use an example, but the information you enter should match what your own ad promises. You'll also need to be signed in, with permission to edit the connection. If you're wondering how to keep both accounts open, that little plus beside your browser tab opens another tab without closing this one. When we get to testing, use your own name and a phone you control, rather than patient information. Let your office know, too, because existing follow-up messages could run when you submit.

fields.label: Account access
fields.value: Patient Pipeline Lead Follow-Up and the source service

fields.label: Test information
fields.value: Your own name and phone; no patient information

scenes.checkpoint: Sign in before continuing. Never show passwords or private links.

scenes.title: Confirm the page and Instant Form
scenes.narration: Before we add anything, let's make sure we're starting from a connection that's already working. In Go High Level, check that you're in the right practice. We need the Facebook Page and exact Instant Form for this offer; write down both names so we can select them later. For Instagram, you'll use the linked Facebook Page. Now find a recent lead from that form in Contacts and check that the name and phone arrived. If they didn't, pause here and fix that first connection. Adding our workflow won't repair a lead that never reaches Go High Level.

fields.label: Contacts
fields.value: Confirm an actual recent lead and phone

scenes.checkpoint: No sample contact shown here is proof that your existing integration works.

scenes.title: Open a new campaign
scenes.narration: Let's start in Patient Pipeline. We're going to use Lead Follow-Up, rather than Reactivation, because we're setting up an offer that brings in new inquiries. Once you're in there, open Campaigns. This is how Patient Pipeline keeps each offer and its leads together, so your caller knows which conversation to have. Go ahead and click New Campaign. That brings us to the offer details. We'll keep using this same campaign for the connection and the test, so we don't end up looking for our test person in the wrong place.
scenes.checkpoint: You should be in Lead Follow-Up, with New Campaign open.

scenes.title: Choose the service
scenes.narration: Now that the offer form is open, the first thing I want you to look at is Service type. Click there to open the choices. I'm choosing Chiropractic because that matches the back pain offer we're using. Yours might be different, and that's completely fine. Just choose the service your ad is actually promoting, because that's what helps Patient Pipeline choose the right call script. Have a quick look at what's selected before we start typing the rest of the offer. We want the script to match the service, not just the name we're about to give it.
scenes.checkpoint: The selected service must match your ad.

scenes.title: Type a recognizable name
scenes.narration: Now that we've got the service selected, let's give the campaign a name your team will recognize. I'll click Campaign name and type Back Pain Relief, forty-nine-dollar New Patient Special. You don't have to use that wording. The important thing is that when someone on your team sees this name later, they'll know exactly which offer the person asked about. Keeping it specific also makes it easier for us to find the right campaign when we check the connection. Take a moment to enter yours, and then we'll add what the offer includes.

fields.label: Campaign name
fields.value: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

actions.result: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

scenes.checkpoint: Use the same campaign for setup, connection, and testing.

scenes.title: Enter what the offer includes
scenes.narration: Let's tell your caller what the person actually gets with this offer. I'm putting Consultation in the first row. We'll give each included item its own line, rather than squeezing everything into one sentence. To make room for another item, click Add a line. I'll put Examination in that next row, and then add Review of findings underneath it. Those are just our example's inclusions. Before you move on, compare your entries with the ad itself, because these details become part of what your caller says. We don't want to promise something your practice hasn't actually offered.
scenes.checkpoint: One real included item per row.

scenes.title: Choose Just Y, then type 49
scenes.narration: Now let's set the price wording your caller will use. Our example only needs to say what the offer costs, so I'm choosing the middle option, Just Y. Once that's selected, I'll click Offer price and type forty-nine. Have a look at the On the call preview underneath. That's where you can check the wording before anyone uses it. This doesn't change your software bill. If your ad really compares two prices, you'd use Normally X, now Y instead and enter both amounts. For our example, we'll leave this at Just forty-nine dollars.
scenes.checkpoint: Just Y selected • Offer price 49 • Preview Just $49

scenes.title: Save and connect leads
scenes.page: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special
scenes.narration: We've got the offer details in place now. You'll also see a place for an expiration or limited spots. It's fine to leave that blank if your ad doesn't have that restriction; we don't want to invent urgency. Take a moment to look back over what you've entered. When it matches your offer, click Save and Connect Leads. That saves the campaign and takes us to its connection setup. It hasn't connected the form yet, but now we've got the right destination ready. Leave this campaign open, because we're going to come back to it.
scenes.checkpoint: Wait until the saved campaign's connection setup opens.

scenes.title: Copy this campaign's address
scenes.narration: We've saved the campaign, and now we need somewhere for Go High Level to send these leads. Choose Go High Level on this setup page, because that's the service doing the sending in this route. The private address you see belongs to this particular campaign. Click Copy beside it, and we'll take it over to our new workflow. Don't copy the browser's page address instead; that wouldn't tell the workflow where to deliver the lead. I'm hiding the private value here, but you'll paste your own complete address in a moment. Keep it private.
scenes.checkpoint: Copy the special campaign address—not the browser's page URL.

scenes.title: Create a separate workflow
scenes.narration: Let's switch to your Go High Level tab now, and make sure you're in the right practice. Open Automation, then Workflows. We're going to make a separate connection workflow, rather than change any messages you already have running. Click Create Workflow and choose Start from scratch. Once that opens, click the workflow name and type Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline, or a name that identifies your own form. That way, if you need to check this later, you'll know which workflow handles the connection. Next, we'll tell it exactly when it should run.

fields.label: Workflow name
fields.value: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

actions.result: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

scenes.checkpoint: Use a new workflow, not an existing messaging sequence.

scenes.title: Use Facebook Lead Form Submitted
scenes.narration: Here's where this route differs from a form built inside Go High Level. Click Add New Trigger, then search for Facebook Lead Form Submitted. Choose that exact result, not the ordinary Form Submitted trigger. Now add Page Is and choose the connected Facebook Page you wrote down. Under Form Is, choose this offer's exact Instant Form. We want both filters, otherwise another form could send people into the wrong campaign. When those names match your offer, click Save Trigger. Now the workflow knows which incoming Facebook submission should start our sending step.

actions.cue: search for Facebook Lead Form Submitted

scenes.checkpoint: Facebook Lead Form Submitted • Page Is • Form Is

scenes.title: Choose Webhook—not Custom Webhook
scenes.narration: We've told the workflow which submission to watch for. Now we need to tell it what to do with that submission. Click the plus below the trigger to add an action, and type webhook into the search. Choose the ordinary action called Webhook. We don't want Custom Webhook or an inbound webhook here, because we're sending contact information out to Patient Pipeline. If this action isn't available, or your account asks you to pay for access, pause and check that before continuing. Choosing a similar-looking action won't give us the same setup.
scenes.checkpoint: Select the standard outbound Webhook action.

scenes.title: Set POST and paste the address
scenes.narration: Now we're in the sending step. I'll name it Send lead to Patient Pipeline so its purpose is clear when we come back. Under Method, choose POST. That's the sending method this connection expects. Then click the URL box and paste the private campaign address we copied earlier. On Windows, that's Control V; on a Mac, Command V. If you've copied something else since then, just return to Patient Pipeline and copy the address again. Don't type the hidden example shown here. We need your own complete campaign address in this box.
scenes.checkpoint: Method POST • URL is your campaign's full private address.

scenes.title: Save the sending step
scenes.narration: At this point, you might be wondering where to put the name and phone fields. With this standard Webhook action, you don't have to map those ordinary contact fields yourself; it already includes them. So we'll leave Headers empty, and we won't add anything under Custom Data for this basic setup. Review what the action sends before using it with sensitive information. Now click Save Action. Back in the builder, you should have your form trigger followed by this one sending step. We're not adding texts, emails, or calls to this connection workflow.
scenes.checkpoint: One form trigger → one Webhook action. No handwritten JSON.

scenes.title: Allow re-entry, save, and publish
scenes.narration: The sending step is saved, but we still need to let the workflow run. Open Settings and turn on Allow Re-entry for this new workflow. That lets someone submit again after their previous run has finished. Then return to the Builder and click Save. Once it's saved, change Draft to Publish. Those aren't the same thing: saving keeps your instructions, while publishing allows new submissions to use them. If another save indicator appears, click Save again. Check that yours is actually published before we try the form; this demonstration hasn't activated anything in your account.
scenes.checkpoint: Saved AND Published. This demonstration has not activated your account.

scenes.title: Send a new form submission
scenes.narration: Now that the workflow is published, let's send something new through the actual route. Open the ad or its form preview, and make sure it's the same Instant Form we selected. Enter your own first name and phone number, and read the required consent information before submitting once. To check a particular live ad end to end, submit through that actual ad. Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool can help with a setup check, but its sample isn't proof that the live ad works. We're going to follow this new submission, rather than reuse an old contact.
scenes.checkpoint: Use the exact form after publishing. Test-tool data is a separate setup check.

scenes.title: Follow the lead through GoHighLevel
scenes.narration: Let's see whether that new submission made it through the first part. Back in Go High Level, open Contacts and find your test person. Check the phone number, so we know we're following the same submission. Then open your connection workflow's Execution Logs and look for a recent run. Inspect the Webhook step for that contact. Using Test Workflow with an old contact isn't the same check; it skips the new Facebook submission we care about. Once you've found this new person and their run, we'll return to Patient Pipeline and check the campaign.

fields.label: Find your test
fields.value: Match the actual name and phone

scenes.checkpoint: Trace the same new submission, not an unrelated old contact.

scenes.title: Check the receipt, then the lead
scenes.narration: Now let's return to that same campaign in Patient Pipeline and see what happened to your submission. Look for a recent Form submission received message. If it's still waiting, give it a moment and use your browser's refresh button to check again. Once you can see the receipt, open the campaign's Leads tab and look for the name and phone you used. We're matching your actual details here, not just looking for any new row. The illustration shows where to check; it isn't claiming your connection has passed. That confirmation needs to come from your own submission.

fields.label: Latest receipt
fields.value: Waiting for a submission from your form

scenes.checkpoint: No success is assumed. Find your own submission in this campaign.

scenes.title: Recognize a successful repeat test
scenes.narration: If you're testing again and don't see another row, that doesn't necessarily mean something went wrong. Open Lead sources and look under Last twenty received, then match the time to your test. A New lead result means a new entry was created. An Updated lead result can be successful too; that phone was already in this campaign, so Patient Pipeline updated the existing entry. It may not move to the top. If the receipt says Rejected, open it and read the reason before changing settings. That will tell us much more than repeatedly submitting and hoping.

fields.label: New lead
fields.value: A new campaign lead was created

fields.label: Updated lead
fields.value: Same campaign + same phone may update the existing lead

fields.label: Rejected
fields.value: Open the receipt and read the reason

scenes.checkpoint: Status explanations—not a fabricated delivery log.

scenes.title: Don't mistake an internal test for proof
scenes.page: Only want to check our side?
scenes.narration: There's one distinction I want to make before we finish, because it's easy to mistake a partial test for the whole connection working. Patient Pipeline's internal test checks its own intake. Testing a sending action checks that step, and it may create a real lead, but neither proves the actual form will trigger it automatically. That's why we've started our final check at the form itself and followed that same person's details into the campaign. Let your caller know which entry was your setup test, and keep private details out of any troubleshooting screenshots you share.

fields.label: Connector action test
fields.value: Can send real data; does not prove the trigger

scenes.checkpoint: Keep private details out of screenshots and shared troubleshooting messages.

scenes.title: Find which connection needs attention
scenes.narration: If something is missing, we can narrow it down by where the lead stopped. When the test never reaches Go High Level, look at the existing Facebook integration, permissions, Page and form selection, and name and phone mapping. The owner may need to restore leads access. When the test is in Go High Level but not Patient Pipeline, look at our new workflow's filters, published status, and execution. If its Webhook failed, check POST and the campaign address. Fix that first missing part, then submit again. There's no need to disconnect an integration that's already working.

fields.label: Present in GoHighLevel
fields.value: Check trigger filters and published workflow

fields.label: Webhook failed
fields.value: Check POST and the campaign destination

scenes.title: Before you call it ready
scenes.narration: Before you leave the setup, take one more look at your campaign. Does it match the offer people actually saw? Good. Now make sure the connection is watching the right form and is switched on. The important part is what happened after you activated it: you submitted that actual form, and you found the matching receipt and lead in this campaign. If either part is missing, go back to that point before calling it ready. Leave the connection active, and let your team know which entry was your test. You now know where to look if a future delivery needs attention.
